text: Android: no pull-to-refresh / manual sync + no sync recency indicator
relates: T-32 — both add a sync-state surface; coordinate so there's one 'last synced / pending / failing' component, not two.

Done in 983e115. Built on T-47's SyncStatus holder (coordinated, one surface).

Material PullToRefreshBox on ListScreen + Overview -> immediate foreground
SyncEngine sync with the standard spinner (isRefreshing per UI state; empty states
wrapped in verticalScroll so the pull gesture still fires with nothing to scroll).
Last-synced line: reused SyncStatusBar with a new showAttention=false flag on the
list screen (recency only; Overview keeps the loud attention banner). Both read the
SyncStatus StateFlow from T-47.

Design seam: ViewModels depend on a Syncer fun interface, not the concrete
SyncEngine, so screen/VM tests pass a trivial fake instead of building the whole
engine (API client + DataStore + Room). Gotcha hit + resolved: a fun interface
method can't declare a default arg, and an override can't add one either — so
rather than have SyncEngine implement Syncer (which would force every existing
no-arg syncEngine.syncNow() caller to change), Syncer.syncNow has no default and a
thin @Provides adapter { engine.syncNow(it) } bridges to SyncEngine's unchanged
default-arg API. Only the two refresh() call sites pass emptyList() explicitly.

Tests: List + Overview refresh() run a sync and clear the refreshing flag; sync
state flows into the list UI. Verified :app:testDebugUnitTest + :app:lintDebug
green. Pull-gesture itself isn't unit-tested (Compose gesture simulation is
brittle); the refresh() wiring it invokes is. Actual on-device pull falls under
T-29's emulator pass.
